baseline.name: Linear scan of the rotated array
baseline.approach: Compare the target with each element until found or exhausted.

why: Distinct values let each iteration identify a sorted half and eliminate a half that cannot contain the target.
quantitative_comparison: An unsuccessful linear scan checks n elements. Binary search performs at most floor(log2(n))+1 iterations for n>0, with several comparisons per iteration. The iteration bound improves; no fixed ratio of machine instructions or elapsed time follows.
tradeoffs: Requires a rotated sorted array with distinct values. The simpler linear scan works without that structural assumption.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
